title: When does "only a few left" work?
principle: Scarce things feel more valuable. Only claim scarcity that is true.

screens.text: Let me tell you about a phone. On 2 December 2014, the OnePlus One went on sale in India. You could buy it only on Amazon, and you needed an invite. Why make it so hard to buy? A study about cookies helps explain.

screens.prompt: In a 1975 study, people tasted the same cookies from two jars. One had 10 cookies, the other had 2. Which did they like more?

options.label: Both jars had equally good cookies

screens.why: They liked the cookies from the jar with 2 more. The cookies were the same, but having fewer made them feel more special.

screens.title: Scarcity
screens.text: This is called scarcity. When something is hard to get, we want it more. In the same study, a third group had their jar go from 10 cookies to 2 just before tasting, and they liked the cookies most of all. The OnePlus invites worked on the same feeling.

screens.title: It's used on you
screens.text: You see this often: "only 2 rooms left, 30 people looking", timers counting down, and "limited stock". Some claims are true, but many are not. In 2023, India's consumer authority banned "false urgency": saying stock or time is running out when it isn't.

screens.title: Now look at your business
screens.text: A phone and a home bakery seem very different, but you've seen this go wrong. In June, you posted "Only 5 cakes left!" twice. After that, the new colony stopped ordering for a while. Now Christmas plum cakes bring your biggest order of the year.

screens.title: A real limit
screens.text: Fruit for plum cakes must soak for weeks. In November, you soaked enough fruit for 40 cakes, and no more. So you can sell only 40 this Christmas. Each cake sells for ₹1,200 and costs ₹600 to make. This limit is real.

screens.prompt: True or false: Saying "Only 40 plum cakes" is fair, even if you could have made 80 but chose to make 40.

options.label: True: a limit I chose is still real
False: only limits I can't change count

screens.why: True. You chose to make 40, and you'll make exactly 40. The limit is real, so saying it is honest. False urgency means claiming a limit that isn't real.

wrong.b: A limit you choose is still real if you keep it. Many bakers choose how many cakes to make. False urgency means claiming a limit that isn't real.

screens.prompt: You must stop taking orders in time to bake every cake before Christmas. Which post is honest?

options.label: "Only 3 left!" in every post, all month

screens.why: Exactly. The number and date are both real, and you said them clearly. Buyers can plan without feeling cheated.

wrong.a: Saying "Only 3 left" every day for a month is false. Buyers notice, like the mother in June did. Tell them the real limit: 40 cakes, orders close 20 December.
wrong.b: That time limit is false. Nothing changes in 10 minutes. Buyers who feel forced may decide not to buy. Tell them the real limit: 40 cakes, orders close 20 December.

screens.prompt: I'll show you six messages. For each one, tell me: is the limit real, or is it false urgency?

items.text: "40 cakes only", when you soaked fruit for 40
A timer that counts down but starts again every day
"6 seats in my baking class", and your kitchen fits 6
"Only 2 left!" when you could bake 20 more
"Orders close 20 December", so every cake is ready for Christmas
"30 people are looking right now!" when nobody counted

screens.why: A real limit has a real reason, like fruit, seats or time. A timer that starts again, a fake "only 2 left" or a made-up number of viewers is false urgency. India bans these false claims.

screens.setup: It's 18 December. 34 of your 40 plum cakes are booked, so 6 are left. An office that buys your birthday cakes now wants 20 plum cakes. Each plum cake leaves you ₹600. Each chocolate cake leaves you ₹450.
screens.question: What do you tell the office?

options.label: "Yes, all 20." Make 14 more without soaked fruit
options.outcome: The 14 cakes made in a hurry taste dry. The office pays for the 6 good cakes and returns the 14. Those 14 cost you ₹8,400 to make. After the 6 good cakes, you've lost ₹4,800.
options.why: Your limit was real. Making more cakes without soaked fruit made them worse. A real limit helps you keep your quality.
options.better: Offer the 6 plum cakes and chocolate cakes for the rest.

options.label: "Sorry, we're sold out", and keep the 6 for others
options.outcome: The office buys from another shop. The last 6 plum cakes sell to families by 20 December, leaving you ₹3,600.
options.why: You were honest and kept your limit. But you could have offered the office cakes you were able to make.
options.better: Offer the 6 plum cakes and chocolate cakes for the rest.

options.label: "6 plum cakes left. Chocolate cakes for the rest"
options.outcome: The office buys 6 plum cakes and 14 chocolate cakes. You keep ₹3,600 plus ₹6,300: ₹9,900. The manager asks to book 30 plum cakes in October for next Christmas.
options.why: You kept your real limit and still helped the office. Next year, they'll order early because they trust that your limit is real.

screens.title: The honest line
screens.text: The line one last time: use on others only what you'd accept being used on you. Tell buyers your real limit: how many, and until when. Never make up a limit. False urgency is against the law in India, and buyers who find out may stop trusting you.
Scarce things feel more ___. Only claim scarcity that is ___.
screens.why: Exactly. The invites made the phone hard to get, so it felt special. Your 40 plum cakes also feel special because the number and closing date are real. Buyers don't feel cheated.

summary: Scarcity: when something is hard to get, we want it more.
Tell buyers the real number, closing date and reason for the limit.
False urgency, like fake "only 2 left" claims or timers that restart, is banned in India and makes buyers lose trust.

cards.front: You can make only 40 hampers. Is "Only 40 hampers, orders close Friday" fair?
options: No, every limit is a trick
cards.back: A real limit, stated clearly, is fair.

cards.front: A website shows "Only 2 left!" every day for a month. What is it?
cards.back: India banned false urgency as a dark pattern in 2023.

cards.front: In one study, which jar's cookies did people like more?
cards.back: Things that are hard to get feel more valuable, even when nothing else changes.

sources.label: OnePlus One available in India without an invite on Feb 10 (FoneArena, 2015)
OnePlus One launched in India on December 2, to retail exclusively on Amazon India (Mobigyaan)
Scarcity (social psychology): Worchel, Lee and Adewole's cookie jar study (1975)
Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (CCPA, notified 30 Nov 2023)
